title: Assertion Wrangler collector specification and control-evidence workflow notes
content:
Purpose and scope:

This document defines the Assertion Wrangler collector (AWC) — a lightweight, resilient evidence collector and forwarder designed to capture control assertions, enriched audit events, and periodic compliance snapshots from our fleets (hosted, dedicated, and private deployments) and reliably export them to downstream evidence stores and SIEMs. It specifies message shapes, delivery semantics, RBAC integration (RBAC v2 mapping), retention checkpoints, backfill behavior, and operational runbook fragments for common failure modes.

Goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Provide a minimal on-host collector that emits signed, schema-validated evidence objects for every control assertion (policy-check pass/fail, role-change, privileged operation, config drift, key-material access).
  - Ensure exactly-once visible evidence semantics at the consumer layer (idempotent ingestion keys, monotonic sequence where possible).
  - Support streaming exports to Splunk, Elastic, and SumoLogic via native connectors and to object stores (S3/GCS) for long-term retention.
  - Integrate with RBAC v2 to attach effective-principal context to each evidence record.
- Non-goals:
  - Not a full-featured log ingestion framework (no heavy metrics collection).
  - Not a replacement for centralized telemetry (prometheus traces); AWC focuses on control evidence only.

High-level architecture:
- Collector components:
  1) On-host AWC agent (Go binary) — subscribes to local event sources (auditd, application audit sockets, agent SDK hooks) and the control-plane webhook stream.
  2) Local buffer store — append-only WAL (RocksDB or file-backed) to persist events until acknowledgement from downstream.
  3) Connector plugins — configured at deploy-time: siem-forwarder (TCP/HEC), object-exporter (S3 multipart), kafka-proxy (for Dedicated), and http-exporter (for Private control plane).
  4) Checkpointer — periodic snapshot of last-acked sequence per destination, stored encrypted in agent-config store or control-plane for hosted agents.

Message schema (audit evidence object):
- Top-level fields (all keys are string unless otherwise noted):
  - evidence_id: UUIDv4 string (unique per logical assertion)
  - evidence_type: short tag (e.g., "role_assignment", "policy_evaluation", "config_change", "kv_access")
  - timestamp_utc: ISO8601 timestamp
  - host_id: machine-id or instance-id
  - deployment_scope: one of ["hosted", "dedicated", "private"]
  - principal: principal object flattened as strings (principal_id, principal_type, principal_email)
  - effective_roles: comma-separated list representing RBAC v2 effective role ids at time of event
  - resource: resource path string (e.g., "/v1/models/model-1234/weights")
  - action: canonical action verb (e.g., "read", "write", "deploy", "rollback")
  - result: one of ["success", "failure", "denied"]
  - reason: short free-text for human interpretability (max 1024 chars)
  - related_evidence_ids: comma-separated UUID list (for multi-step flows)
  - sequence_id: monotonic per host integer (string encoded)
  - signature: base64-ed25519(signature over canonicalized payload)
  - schema_version: string (current: "2024-01-aws-1")

Notes on principal and RBAC v2 integration:
- The agent must call the local RBAC library (or host-provided sidecar) to compute effective_roles for the principal at event time. Effective_roles MUST be included for any event that changes access state (role grants/revokes, policy evals that lead to deny).
- Principal fields are to be derived from the authentication token (OIDC subject, service account id) and must include an immutable principal_id (stable GUID).
- For hosted tenants, when the control plane performs role elevation on behalf of tenant admins, agent includes control_plane_actor and actor_context fields (flattened into principal_* fields and additional tag principal_delegated_by).

Delivery guarantees and idempotency:
- Local persistence ensures at-least-once delivery from agent to connector. Downstream consumers must deduplicate using evidence_id and host_id+sequence_id.
- Agent will retry delivery with exponential backoff and jitter.
- For object-exporter (S3): evidence objects are batched per-minute into compressed ndjson files with a manifest file describing first_sequence_id and last_sequence_id for the batch. Manifest signed by agent. This enables idempotent ingest and backfill reconciliation.
- For SIEM-forwarders (Splunk HEC, Elastic ingest API): agent will send each event individually but inject a header X-Evidence-Id and X-Sequence to help SIEMs deduplicate and reindex.

Checkpointing and backfill:
- Checkpointer writes a per-destination checkpoint at least every 30s or after 500 events. Checkpoint record includes last_sequence_id, last_evidence_id, and a wall-clock time.
- If a destination is unavailable for >5m, agent begins batching to object-exporter mode and emits a failure-metadata event to the control plane.
- Backfill: when destination is restored, agent will iterate WAL from last_checkpoint+1 and replay events in original order. Connector-level acknowledgements update checkpoint.

Security and signing:
- All evidence objects emitted by the agent must be signed (ed25519) with a per-host keypair provisioned via the customer KMS or Redwood control-plane CA depending on deployment mode.
- Signature covers canonicalized JSON payload excluding the signature field. Canonicalization = sorted keys, utf-8, no extra whitespace.
- For Private deployments that forbid outbound connections, agent writes signed batches to a customer-configured S3-compatible endpoint in an encrypted bucket with server-side encryption enforced.

Schema evolution and compatibility:
- Fields are additive-only. Any rename triggers new schema_version. Consumers must tolerate unknown fields.
- Agents include schema_version and a compact manifest in every batch. Control plane will run nightly compatibility checks and emit regression alerts to the security channel if incompatible field-level changes are detected.

Operational runbook (common incidents):
1) Destination unreachable (SIEM/HTTP 5xx)
   - Agent enters retry mode (capped window 24h) and switches to batch-to-object-exporter after 5 minutes. Alert type: evidence-export-degraded.
   - Runbook: check destination health, check TLS cert expiry, validate network egress rules (especially for Private). Use /admin/forwarder/status endpoint.
2) Checkpoint drift detected (agent reports overlapping sequence ranges)
   - Likely dual-writer or clock skew. Runbook: pause agent, inspect WAL, ensure single active agent identity per host, rotate host key if necessary, reconcile via control-plane reconcile endpoint which compares manifests and tombstones duplicates.
3) Signature validation failures reported by downstream
   - Could be bad canonicalization or key rotation. Runbook: dump canonical payload, verify with current public key in control-plane key registry, check key rollover timeline.

SIEM export connector specifics:
- Splunk HEC:
  - Use persistent TCP with buffer pooling. HEC token injected via connector config. Add X-Evidence-Id, X-Host-Sequence headers. Batch size 500 events or 2MB.
- Elastic ingest API:
  - Bulk API with action-meta + source lines (ndjson). Use evidence_id as _id to enable idempotency.
- IBM QRadar/SumoLogic:
  - Push using syslog over TLS (RFC5424) for events under 2KB; larger events fallback to HTTP ingest.

Privacy and PII handling:
- Evidence objects must never include raw user PII except service account email when required for auditability. When user PII is involved, the agent must replace raw fields with a stable SHA256 pseudonym and add pii_masked:true.
- A separate pii-mapping-store (encrypted) holds reversible mappings for legal-only access; access controlled via RBAC v2 escalation process.

Testing and validation checklist for rollout:
- Unit tests for canonicalization and signature verification.
- Integration tests that validate idempotent replay to all connector types.
- Chaos tests: network partition and destination downtime simulated for 48h to ensure WAL retention and backfill intact.
- Compliance test: generate policy-evaluation events and validate that effective_roles are present and match RBAC v2 computed results across 10k synthetic principals.

Telemetry and metrics (agent exports):
- evidence.emitted.count, evidence.acked.count, evidence.retry.count, wal.size_bytes, checkpoint.latency_ms. Metrics exposed on /metrics in Prometheus format but are considered operational-only (do not contain evidence content).

Rolling upgrades and agent lifecycle:
- Agents must support zero-downtime upgrade: new binary reads WAL and continues sequence numbering; key rotation handled via control-plane orchestrated staged rollout (old key -> dual-signing -> new key).

Open design questions (for follow-up):
- Should we support cross-host globally monotonic sequence ids for multi-container workflows? (tradeoff: coordination overhead vs ordering guarantees)
- How do we best model "related_evidence_ids" for long-running workflows (e.g., multi-step deploys) to enable efficient search in SIEM without exploding index cardinality?

Appendix: quick example evidence object (ndjson, single line)
{"evidence_id":"e7a2f3f8-6a7a-4d2e-9f1d-9b8b9c321e7a","evidence_type":"policy_evaluation","timestamp_utc":"2024-05-30T18:23:12Z","host_id":"i-0a12b3c4d5e6f7","deployment_scope":"dedicated","principal_id":"princ-42a8","principal_type":"service_account","principal_email":"deploy-bot@acme.example","effective_roles":"infra-admin,model-deployer","resource":"/v1/models/model-0001/deploy","action":"deploy","result":"denied","reason":"policy: no-deploy-to-prod-without-approval","related_evidence_ids":"","sequence_id":"12543","signature":"BASE64SIG==","schema_version":"2024-01-aws-1"}

Next steps / immediate asks:
- Security review: Priya to validate PII masking requirements and edge-case exemptions (legal).
- Infra: Jamal to prototype S3 batched manifest handling and manifest-signing.
- Applied-ML: Luca to generate 10k synthetic principal events for integration test harness.
- Product: confirm list of mandatory evidence types for audit reports (deadline 2024-06-14).

Notes: this is deliberately an agent-centric spec to reduce dependence on central ingestion in early releases (v0.1). Later iterations should expand connector capabilities and add a central reconcile service for cross-host correlation.
